extracted.intended_audience: SIGMOD authors and reproducibility reviewers (database systems researchers submitting artifacts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, submitting, and reviewing artifact packages (code, data, scripts, and experiment descriptions) for SIGMOD Availability & Reproducibility Initiative so that others can reproduce, replicate, and reuse experimental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIGMOD ARI goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight the impact of database research papers; enable easy dissemination of research results; enable easy sharing of code and experimentation set-ups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to build a culture where sharing results, code, and scripts is the norm; the committee coordinates with PVLDB Reproducibility to encourage sharing and cross-validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artifact submission contents (minimum required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission should contain: (1) A prototype system as a white box (source, configuration files, build environment) or a fully-specified black-box system; (2) Input Data: either the process to generate input data or the actual data/link; (3) The set of experiments (system configuration and initialization, scripts, workload, measurement protocol) used to produce the raw experimental data; (4) For full reproducibility submissions, the scripts needed to transform the raw data into the graphs included in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing these artifacts earns the 'Artifacts Available' badge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artifacts Evaluated - Reusable criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Artifacts that significantly exceed minimal functionality and are clearly documented, well-structured, and facilitate reuse are awarded the 'Artifacts Evaluated - Reusable' badge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality above minimal functionality + clear documentation + structure + facilitation of reuse are required; reviewers assess these aspects during availability evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results Reproduced criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The central results and claims of the paper should be supported by the submitted experiments so reviewers can recreate result data and graphs that demonstrate similar behavior to those in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact numbers are not expected (hardware differences); expect similar overall behavior and conclusions (e.g., relative performance trends). Successful independent reproduction awards the 'Results Reproduced' badge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Artifact award factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers eligible for Best Artifact are evaluated on: Reproducibility (ideal: all results can be verified), Ease of Reproducibility (ideal: just works), Portability (ideal: linux, mac, windows), Replicability (ideal: can change workloads/queries/data and get similar behavior to published results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are selected by a Reproducibility Awards Committee based on reviewer scores for all listed factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability reviewer's role
rubrics_metrics.description: An artifacts reviewer compiles, deploys, and tests the artifacts and communicates directly with authors to resolve issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ultimate goal is to resolve issues so that all artifacts are made publicly available; availability review is the first phase before reproducibility review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility review process
rubrics_metrics.description: After availability review, each paper is reviewed by one database group; the process occurs in communication with authors and reviewers to fix lingering technical issues and results in a short reproducibility report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For successful papers the reproducibility report is maintained on the Reproducibility Reports page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should explicitly specify the OS and tools required to run the artifacts, including dependencies on specific hardware features (e.g., 25 GB RAM) or intra-environment dependencies (e.g., specific compiler and OS version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail so reviewers can set up the environment; include exact versions and any special hardware requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: System setup automation and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: System setup should be automatic rather than manual; documentation must detail every step: how to obtain the system, how to configure the environment (env vars, paths), how to compile the system (compilation options), how to use the system (configuration options and parameters), and how to verify correct installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scripts that download needed components, initialize the environment, check compatibility, and deploy the system. Authors should test installation in a new environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unavailable/raw-data acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: If raw data acquisition requires special hardware or is infeasible to reproduce, provide a protocol that includes detailed procedures for system set-up, experiment set-up, and measurements rather than raw acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When raw data cannot be produced, the committee will accept detailed acquisition protocols so reviewers understand how data were obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended tooling for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee strongly suggests using tools that capture environment, inputs, outputs, and required libraries in a container-like suite: Docker containers, ReproZip, Jupyter Notebook, GitHub repositories with clear README files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cloud deployment is required, suggest using CloudLab or Chameleon Cloud; the committee can work with authors if tools are difficult to use; more tools listed at reproduciblescience.org directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment completeness and phases
rubrics_metrics.description: For each system, authors should provide the complete set of experiments consisting of: a setup phase (parameters configured and data loaded), a running phase (workload applied and measurements taken), and a clean-up phase (prepare system for next round).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how to perform setup/running/clean-up and how to check these phases complete as they should; document expected effects of setup (e.g., cold cache) and steps/command-line options used in the running phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment automation (scripts with parameterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments should be automatic via scripts that accept a range of values for each experiment parameter rather than requiring manual edits to scripts to set parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automation reduces human error and facilitates reproducibility across parameter sweeps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphs and plots reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For each graph in the paper, authors should describe how the graph is obtained from experimental measurements and include the scripts (or spreadsheets) used to generate the graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide scripts for all graphs when possible; any plotting tool may be used (Gnuplot, Matlab, Matplotlib, R, Octave).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal reproducibility submission (master script)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal submission includes a master script that installs all needed systems, generates or fetches all input data, reruns all experiments and generates all results, generates all graphs and plots, and recompiles the paper sources to produce a new PDF with the new graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is achievable and strongly encouraged; at a minimum provide complete scripts to install the system, produce the data, run experiments, produce resulting graphs, and a detailed README describing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and dispute policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If problems appear during reproducibility testing, the committee will contact authors to work with them; reproducibility failures are not made public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can fix issues in collaboration with the committee; there is no public downside to submitting and attempting reproducibility.
